summary: no forced win for either side within 24 (White) / 22 (Black) plies; game value still open
machine: The WHITE depth-24 bound was measured on an Apple M5 Pro, 18 cores, 64 GiB, macOS (Darwin 25.6.0). The BLACK depth-22 bound is older and was taken on an Apple M2 Pro, 10 cores, 16 GiB, macOS 15 (Darwin 25.5.0) under an earlier build, so the two node counts are not comparable with each other.
note: Two claim strengths, not one. A reported mate is a proof of a forced win and, since the TT_BUDGET_GUARD in tinyhouse.c, of the distance it names: the search returns an unsound 0 at the horizon, so a mate score can only come from real terminals. A 'no forced win within N plies' bound is immune to horizon unsoundness, to a TT cutoff overrunning its budget and to store-side graph-history interaction, but not to a 64-bit Zobrist collision, which has no directional structure and could prune a subtree holding a real mate. That residual is unquantified rather than zero; re-run under a second --seed to check it. Deeper bounds: run solve_hunt.py (see README).
reproducibility: The node counts above are NOT exactly reproducible and are not claimed to be. solve_hunt.py defaulted to 2 workers when these runs were made and lazy SMP is nondeterministic, so the worker count in force is not reliably recorded; the default is 1 now, which is deterministic. A cold single-depth run also differs from the iteratively-deepened slice recorded here (a re-run measured +3.4%). The CLAIMS do not depend on any of this: a null-window hunt returning 0 proves the negative whatever the thread count. Reproduce with: solve_hunt.py 0 --tt 30 --workers 16 --maxdepth 24  /  solve_hunt.py 1 --tt 27 --maxdepth 22 (the Black line reproduces the OLD bound; it has not been re-run on the current build or machine).
